in_sanskrit.name: मधव
in_sanskrit.meaning: sweet, delicious, nectar, honey, God, Lord Vishnu
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: मधु (madhu) + वान (vana) = मधव (madhava) Madhu means 'sweet, delicious, nectar, honey'. Vana means 'forest, wood, abode'. Madhab is a compound word, derived from the combination of Madhu (sweet) and Vana (forest). It can mean 'sweet, delicious, nectar, honey', 'God', or 'Lord Vishnu'. It is a common name for both males and females in Hindu culture.

in_hindi.name: मधव
in_hindi.meaning: मधुकार (madhukar) - स्वादिष्ट (swadisht) वाला मधुकार (madhukar) means 'one who is filled with nectar, or sweet'. Swadisht (swadisht) means 'wished, desired'. So, Madhab can be translated to 'one who is filled with the desired nectar'.
in_hindi.long_meaning: मधु (madhu) + कार (kar) = मधुकार (madhukar) Madhu means 'sweet, delicious, nectar, honey'. Kar means 'doer, maker'. Madhukar is a compound word, derived from the combination of Madhu (sweet) and Kar (doer). It means 'one who is filled with nectar, or sweet'. Swadisht (swadisht) means 'wished, desired'. So, Madhab can be translated to 'one who is filled with the desired nectar'.

in_tamil.name: மதப்
in_tamil.meaning: மது (madhu) + ஆப் (app) மது (madhu) means 'sweet, delicious, nectar, honey'. ஆப் (app) is a suffix that is used to form nouns in Tamil. So, Madhab can be translated to 'sweetness, nectar'.

in_telugu.name: ಮెదేశ
in_telugu.meaning: మెద్దు (meddu) + శేశ (shesham) మెద్దు (meddu) means 'sweet, delicious'. శేశ (shesham) means 'Lord, God'. So, Madhab can be translated to 'sweet Lord, delicious God'.
